_comment: Matches the REAL existing 'USA' tab column layout in your tracker exactly (verified against your uploaded file) — this tab already exists with real rows, so ensure_sheet() never recreates it; legend_row/columns below just document the real layout for reference and for the (unlikely) case the tab needs to be rebuilt from scratch.
_review_status_note: 'Review Status' is a NEW trailing column added for the two-phase flow (email-read-and-append, then a human sets this to Reviewed, then invoice+email get generated). Appended at the end of the real sheet, after 'Amount Tobe transfered' — added by me via script, not by hand, so ask me before assuming it's there if you haven't seen me confirm the sync.
_mis_verified_note: 'MIS Verified' (2026-08-12) is set by the real MIS project-info API call made right when the row is appended (see src/mis/mis_api.py) — True only if that call actually succeeded for the row's PF ID; False (never blocks the append) if the API failed, timed out, or the token was expired, so accounts knows to check that project ID by hand.
_currency_note: 'Currency' (2026-08-13) is a NEW trailing column, per explicit instruction ('you just add the column named currency, no logic for now'). No extraction logic was built yet — every new row gets this tab's 'default_currency' (USD) below, same value the PDF/email already use today via config/entities/usa.json; nothing changes about what currency is actually billed. Historical rows are left blank here, same policy as every other trailing column added so far.
_company_address_resource_description_no: 2026-09-28: corrected a drift between this file and the real live sheet -- the real 'USA' tab had already split the single 'Company Name and Address' column into separate 'Company Name'/'Company Address' columns and added a 'Resource Description' column (used by the dedicated-invoice-generation flow's consolidated resource list), but this schema was never updated to match. That drift caused save_invoice() to write a row's values into the wrong physical columns (everything from 'Company Name' onward landed one-to-two columns off). Fixed here, and excel_writer.py's save_invoice() now resolves each column by matching live header text instead of trusting this array's position, so a future drift fails loudly (SchemaDriftError) instead of silently misplacing data.
